city_metadata.subtitle: Evidence map from GitHub/paper arXiv:2609.11975
city_metadata.scale_axis_description: Following the paper's own Figure 1: what was counted, which design cell stays empty, how six rules fared when tested on new cases, and how papers and code connect. Limitations sit on the finding they weaken.

districts.name: 1 · THE POPULATION
districts.description: What was counted: 139 canonical public repositories admitted through unequal discovery channels — agents, benchmarks, libraries, substrates, lists and boundary artifacts. Nine lineages cover only 52 of them. Estimating how many runnable agents exist needs a separate role-coding pass.

districts.name: 2 · THE DESIGN SPACE
districts.scale_label: One cell stays empty — even after a 962-repository re-test
districts.description: RQ1. Every record is coded on selection signal × judge. Most compare candidates with a strict scalar; 38 run no comparison and no gate at all; and no clean optimization loop keeps a vector signal with a language-model judge. A post-freeze sweep found the closest miss, an unreachable pool and an untestable candidate — three routes by which the cell stays empty.

districts.name: 3 · THE THEORY ON TRIAL
districts.scale_label: Six rules fixed in advance · 0 of 6 triggers fired
districts.description: RQ2. Six candidate regularities were written down with trigger observations on 17 May 2026, then 25 new repositories were inspected. No trigger fired, which gives bounded support only: R1 and R3 hold, R2 and R4 are conditional, R5's broad form is contradicted and R6 stays exploratory.

districts.name: 4 · PAPERS ↔ CODE
districts.scale_label: 212 edges map our curation, not citation
districts.description: RQ3. 64 of 101 papers are coded as related to at least one repository, but the edges reach only 23 of 139 repositories, and six hubs carry 56.6% of them. A full-text sample found a mention for 3 of 29 edges, so this is a map of the curation. At least 18 paper authors also commit to a registry repository.

spires.title: Repository registry
spires.abstract: 139 canonical public GitHub records after three aliases are folded into their targets. Roles span research agents, benchmarks, libraries, substrates, meta-resources, paper companions and boundary artifacts, so 139 counts public artifacts, not runnable agents; estimating agent prevalence needs a separate role-coding pass. Every record carries an agent-drafted, human-adjudicated evidence card (141 cards; the two extra are explained) anchored to its primary sources.

spires.title: Nine promoted lineages
spires.abstract: Seed-line 19, dr-deep-research-agent 10, rl-post-training-as-autoresearch 8, multi-agent-scientist 7, clune-lab-open-endedness 5, mlagentbench-derived 4, camel-ai-line 2, dspy-line 2, physical-robotic-automation 2. 87 registry records have no lineage. The relation mixes code ancestry, shared infrastructure, intellectual influence and structural convergence.

spires.title: Records in no lineage
spires.abstract: Nine promoted lineages cover 52 of the 139 canonical records; the remaining 87 have no promoted-lineage membership. The lineage map is a structured, overlapping view of a subset, not a partition of the registry.

spires.title: Curated lists
spires.abstract: Two existing curated lists supplied 83 of the 139 canonical repository records: 75 from the larger seed list and 8 from a second list. Channels are unequal in yield, which is why the registry is an engineered discovery sample rather than a census.

spires.title: Synthesis passes
spires.abstract: Synthesis passes combined snowball search over already-inspected repositories with targeted GitHub search. No record entered through undirected GitHub search alone; GitHub search is a technique inside these passes, not a channel.

spires.title: Paper references, leaderboard and other channels
spires.abstract: Fifteen records came from references in papers, nine from a public benchmark leaderboard, one from a pull request against a curated list and one from a direct recommendation. No record entered through undirected GitHub search alone.

spires.title: Coding primitives A1–A5

metrics.acceleration: Unit of work · signal · judge · pattern · antipattern
metrics.maturity: 0 contradictions in 176 bindings on the four cell axes

spires.abstract: A1 unit of work, A2 selection signal (strict scalar, band-tolerant, vector, relational, none), A3 judge (programmatic, language-model, hybrid, absent), A4 pattern and A5 antipattern under a recorded promotion rule. The null position is the second most common value on both axes; 38 records take it on both.

spires.title: Artifact-level check of the codings

metrics.maturity: Strong on cell axes, weak on patterns and cost

spires.abstract: Two layers: every revision-pinned anchor was fetched at its revision (3306 of 3547 resolve to a verbatim line), and 538 load-bearing codings over 44 repositories and 10 papers were each paired with a verbatim fact. Selection signal, judge type, loop topology and tool category carry zero contradictions across 176 bindings — the axes this plaza and R3 rest on.

spires.title: Post-freeze re-test of the empty cell
spires.abstract: 962 repositories created after the freeze, 319 retained by a mechanical filter, 69 flagged by triage agents, 15 highest-stakes flags re-checked by agents told to default to refutation: 11 refuted. The cell stays empty, now by three routes, with one case that shows what filling it would require.

spires.title: virtual-biotech-scientist
spires.abstract: Six single-axis language-model judges score each candidate against the incumbent; verdicts are kept as a six-element vector and front membership is gated by a unanimity dominance predicate with no scalar reduction. The front is built once and never feeds a later generation — whether that fills the cell is the open adjudication.

spires.title: XScientist
spires.abstract: A complete and correct seven-dimension Pareto pool that no live path reaches: the reviewer emits a flat score object while the pool's only writer expects a nested one. Executing the repository's own chain admits nothing — the third route by which the cell stays empty.

spires.title: AgenticOperator
spires.abstract: The candidate recorded in advance as most likely to fill the cell. Re-probed on 26 July 2026 across five repository-name variants and the author's homepage: no code release found.

spires.title: Prospective audit
spires.abstract: Six candidate regularities and their minimum trigger observations were time-stamped at a 76-record baseline before 25 newly ingested repositories were inspected in June 2026. None of the six trigger events occurred; trigger absence supplies bounded support, and corpus-wide evidence is reported as a separate layer.

spires.title: Pattern-strength ranking (Tier S)
spires.abstract: Tier S: judge-uncalibrated, staged-validation-before-judge, scoreboard, eval-discipline-regression, keep-or-revert — two antipatterns, two architectures, one component under every weighting. Which pattern leads depends on the weighting and on the lineage relation used.

spires.title: Pattern compendium
spires.abstract: Promoted records: 22 architectures, 7 components, 16 coding patterns and 9 antipatterns. 38 rest on two or more independently inspected artifacts; 16 rest on exactly one and were promoted for structural distinctness or portability — so totals count promoted records, not twice-confirmed regularities.

spires.title: Paper registry (101 records)
spires.abstract: 101 curated records (98 unique artifacts). 64 carry at least one curator-assigned relatedness edge (63.4%, 95% CI 53.5–72.3); under adversarial imputation of the 25 records without full text the rate lies in [63.4%, 88.1%]. Fifteen papers have a companion-code URL resolving to a canonical repository.

spires.title: Authorship audit

metrics.maturity: Lower bound only on commit tier

spires.abstract: Display-name equality nominates a case; confirmation needs an explicit source and a second pass against complete commit histories. At least 18 identities (20 of 63 slots, 13 of 101 papers) are commit-adjudicated; the byline tier of 58 is attributed credit, not a bound.

bottlenecks.title: Engineered discovery sample
bottlenecks.impact: Search terms, curated lists, snowballing, GitHub availability and English-language metadata shaped what entered; global prevalence lies outside the design.
bottlenecks.remedy: Declare the unit of analysis; role-code artifacts and state an explicit sampling frame before prevalence estimates.

bottlenecks.title: Private use unmeasured
bottlenecks.impact: Private deployments lie outside both sampling frames; their size and behaviour are unmeasured.
bottlenecks.remedy: Surveys, consent-based telemetry or institutional sampling.

bottlenecks.title: Single coder, no double coding
bottlenecks.impact: Coding stayed single-coder; the artifact check shows whether a coding is demonstrable, not whether a second coder would agree. Artifact roles and several design variables lack independent double coding.
bottlenecks.remedy: Independent double coding with reported inter-rater agreement; separate the lineage sub-relations.

bottlenecks.title: Two coding families contradicted
bottlenecks.impact: Pattern membership (10 of 64 bindings contradicted) feeds the ranking's support counts; iteration-cost coordinates (10 of 59) feed the cost-versus-ambition matrix — the two weakest results.
bottlenecks.remedy: Re-code both families against primary sources before using them as counts.

bottlenecks.title: Single-agent triage is unreliable
bottlenecks.impact: Fifteen independent re-checks told to default to refutation overturned 11 of the 15 highest-stakes trigger flags — the calibration to attach to any single-agent trigger report.
bottlenecks.remedy: Adversarial multi-route re-checks before counting a trigger.

bottlenecks.title: nexus-swarm: open case for R1
bottlenecks.impact: A mutated prompt is accepted on an uncalibrated judge's self-reported score with no programmatic co-gate. If the mutation is on the causal path of the score it bears on R1; if not, it is a different failure — a gate that fires while the mutation is inert.
bottlenecks.remedy: Establish whether the mutated artifact lies on the causal path of the scored scalar.

bottlenecks.title: No code release found
bottlenecks.impact: The most likely candidate for the empty cell exists only as a paper; nothing can be executed.

bottlenecks.title: Non-random audit, no external preregistration
bottlenecks.impact: The audit has 25 non-random cases; its protocol was time-stamped in project history without external preregistration governance, and several variables lacked double coding.
bottlenecks.remedy: Externally preregistered triggers and a random draw of new cases.

bottlenecks.title: Ranking computed at the baseline
bottlenecks.impact: The ranking was computed at the 76-record baseline; ranks two to five were not recomputed after the audit, and a full re-walk is deferred.
bottlenecks.remedy: Re-walk the ranking against the 139-record corpus.

bottlenecks.title: Architecture leads under nine lineages
bottlenecks.impact: Under the nine promoted lineage records keep-or-revert (an architecture) leads in two of four weightings — 16.8 vs 16.5 baseline, 19.0 vs 16.0 linear — through one contested repository, ML-Agent.
bottlenecks.remedy: Adjudicate contested supporting repositories; report both lineage relations.

bottlenecks.title: judge-uncalibrated spans four lineages
bottlenecks.impact: An evaluation failure occurs in four lineages that share no architecture, while architecture patterns appear in at most two — contradicting the broad form of R5.
bottlenecks.remedy: Treat evaluation infrastructure as a cross-lineage risk: immutable evaluation code and shipped calibration artifacts.

bottlenecks.title: Runtime-contract stayed at three
bottlenecks.impact: The directional companion prediction G1 expected a fourth runtime-contract instance; the count stayed at three across 15 recorded observations.
bottlenecks.remedy: Survival or event-history analysis over a sequence of frozen snapshots.

bottlenecks.title: Relatedness is not citation
bottlenecks.impact: Full text of seven linked papers was searched for the 29 repositories they are credited with: 3 locatable (one in prose, two in references), 26 not. The graph maps the curation, not the papers' citation behaviour.
bottlenecks.remedy: A mention extraction over the 76 records with retrievable full text, admitting only locatable mentions, to build a comparable citation graph.

bottlenecks.title: Papers without full text
bottlenecks.impact: Twenty-five paper records had no accessible full text; under adversarial imputation the paper-side incidence lies in [63.4%, 88.1%].
bottlenecks.remedy: Retrieve full text before coding relatedness.

bottlenecks.title: Byline tier is not a bound
bottlenecks.impact: 40 of 63 byline-matched slots come from four records that transcribe the paper's own author list; commit histories cannot support at least 24 of the 63.
bottlenecks.remedy: Count only commit-adjudicated identities as a lower bound; keep the byline tier separate.

challenges.title: Structural compatibility constrains failure modes
challenges.target: Structural commitments remove specific failure modes from the design surface. Four zero co-occurrence pairs at baseline; the one new seed-line case in the audit used programmatic acceptance, so the P1 trigger (seed-line with an uncalibrated language-model judge) was not observed.

challenges.title: Iteration cost rises with artifact openness
challenges.target: Fast iteration co-occurs with bounded, programmatically scored artifacts. Empty forbidden quadrant if only measured durations count — but the open-ended column then holds no measurement at all; two open-ended repositories bound an iteration below ten minutes if configured bounds count.

challenges.title: The vector-signal / LM-judge cell stays empty
challenges.target: No clean optimization loop keeps a vector signal and a language-model judge. At least 23 adjacent or refused landings; three routes keep the cell empty: refused on evaluation cost, escaped through tournament aggregation, shipped unreachable.

challenges.title: Failure patterns lead the evidence ranking
challenges.target: An antipattern leads the composite ranking under the imported four-lineage relation; under the nine promoted lineages an architecture pattern leads in two of four weightings. Tier S membership is stable, the leading position is not.

challenges.title: Unit of work constrains cross-lineage transfer
challenges.target: Proposed: design patterns stay local to one or two lineages. No migration occurred in the audit, but judge-uncalibrated spans four lineages; restricting the claim to architecture patterns came after the counterexample and is post hoc.

challenges.title: Long-stagnant patterns rarely jump
challenges.target: No long-stagnant two-instance pattern jumped to five; the directional companion prediction G1 failed (runtime-contract stayed at three across 15 observations).

highlight.label: R3 · ≥23 NEAR, 0 CLEAN
highlight.note: Not a surprising zero by count — only two records use a vector signal (expected 0.47 here), and both use a programmatic scorer. R3 rests on design attempts: at least 23 systems landed in adjacent designs and none built a clean optimization loop that keeps a vector of LLM judgments; the post-freeze re-test found a case that meets two of three clauses.

tour.title: 139 artifacts — not 139 agents
tour.text: A registry of 139 public repositories and 101 papers, frozen on 10 June 2026. Only 84 are coded as agents; the rest are lists, substrates, benchmarks, libraries and tools. Before looking at new data, the authors also wrote down six rules about how such systems are built — the blank board here; the tour will put them on trial.
tour.look: The roles plaza (84 agents vs 55 other artifacts) and the blank board of six rules

tour.title: The empty cell
tour.text: Every record is coded by how it compares candidates and who judges them. Most use one scalar judged by code; 38 compare nothing and judge nothing. One cell stays empty: no system keeps a vector of LLM judgments — the two vector systems use code as judge, and three LLM-judged ones escape into tournament scoring. This absence is R3, one of the six rules (stop 4).
tour.look: The fenced 'R3 · ≥23 near, 0 clean' cell with its 'exp 0.47', the 'TOURNAMENT · 3' neighbour, and the hatched judge-absent row

tour.title: 962 repositories later
tour.text: A post-freeze sweep tried to fill the cell. The closest miss meets two of three clauses; one repository ships a Pareto pool no code path reaches; the candidate predicted in advance has no code. Of 15 hits flagged by triage agents, 11 were wrong.
tour.look: The scaffolded tower, two ghosts, and the '11 of 15 refuted' chip

tour.title: Rules written before looking
tour.text: The six rules and their trigger events were fixed on 17 May; then 25 new repositories were inspected and none of the six triggers fired. That is bounded support, not proof — and broader evidence still moved two rules and broke one:
tour.look: Six target pins coloured by verdict; the board in district 1 now shows the verdicts

items.text: R3 · no loop keeps LLM-judged vectors
R5 · patterns stay in their lineage

tour.title: It depends on what you count
tour.text: R2 says fast iteration only comes with bounded artifacts. Count measured times only, and the forbidden cell is empty — because open-ended systems publish no measurements. Count configured limits too, and two counterexamples appear.
tour.look: Table 7 switched to rule (b): the red-fenced cell now holds 2

tour.title: Failures travel, architectures don't
tour.text: The uncalibrated LLM judge shows up in four lineages, while architecture patterns stay within one or two. Evaluation infrastructure carries failures across otherwise unrelated systems; the broad form of R5 is contradicted.
tour.look: The red R5 pin and the '4 lineages' chip on the Tier S ranking

tour.title: Six hubs — on our map
tour.text: 64 of 101 papers are linked to only 23 repositories, and six hubs carry 56.6% of the 212 edges. In a full-text sample only 3 of 29 credited repositories are actually mentioned: the graph shows the curators' view, not citations.
tour.look: Six skyscraper hubs and their roads; the 'not a citation' tape around the district

tour.title: What would change the picture
tour.text: Fill the empty cell in a controlled experiment of scalar, vector and tournament variants; extract real mentions to turn the curated graph into a citation graph; role-code the registry to count actual agents.
